note: Row-count assertions, not smoke tests. On Databend a mistranslated query returns zero rows and raises no error, so 'the SQL executed' proves nothing. Every case here states a relationship between two counts. Baselines are relative, so the suite stays valid as the table grows.

cases.name: empty search returns everything
cases.note: The whole reason this project exists. match(msg,'') returns 0 rows silently, and the optimiser pushes match() into the index scan regardless of the surrounding boolean, so an empty box must compile to SQL containing no match() at all.

cases.name: AND narrows
cases.note: Adjacency means AND, so adding a term can only shrink the result set. If this ever exceeds the baseline, the default operator has silently become OR. The pair must be one that genuinely co-occurs: with disjoint terms the intersection is legitimately 0, and 0 passes any upper-bound assertion — so this uses `narrows`, which also requires the count to be nonzero.

cases.name: phrase is order-sensitive
cases.note: Positions are stored: 72,601 rows for this phrase against 0 for the reversed one when measured.

cases.name: reversed phrase finds nothing
cases.note: Negative control for the case above. If this is ever nonzero, phrase search has degenerated to an unordered token AND.

cases.name: fuzzy typo matches the baseline
cases.note: The headline fix. Typed as Lucene `snapshoot~1` this returns 0 through query(); compiled to match(msg,'snapshoot','fuzziness=1') it returns the baseline and a little more (measured 17,341 against 17,336) because other tokens also sit within one edit of the stem. Hence 'at least the baseline', not equality.

cases.name: fuzziness is bounded
cases.note: Two edits from the stem, rejected at fuzziness=1. Guards against fuzzy matching degenerating into match-anything. NOTE: edit distance is measured against the STEM, not the typed word.

cases.name: two edits accepted at fuzziness 2
cases.note: Measured 17,321 against a 17,316 baseline: fuzziness=2 matches a few extra tokens, so the assertion is 'at least the baseline', not equality.

cases.name: prefix wildcard works via LIKE
cases.note: Through query() the star is silently ignored and `snapsh*` returns 0 while `snapshot*` returns the full baseline, which looks like success. Compiled to LIKE 'snapsh%' it returns real rows.

cases.name: negation excludes
cases.note: MUST-VERIFY. Negating a match() relies on the optimiser handling an inverted-index scan under NOT. §5.1 showed match() pushdown does not always respect the surrounding boolean, so this is the case most likely to expose an engine bug rather than a compiler bug. Asserted as an exact partition of the baseline rather than an upper bound, because NOT swallowing the whole predicate yields 0, which is also <= the baseline.

cases.name: negation of an absent term changes nothing
cases.note: Sharper than the case above: excluding a term that matches nothing must leave the count untouched. If this comes back 0, NOT is swallowing the whole predicate.

cases.name: structured filter is case-insensitive
cases.note: Databend has no ILIKE, so case-insensitivity is compiled explicitly with lower() on both sides.

cases.name: hyphen is not negation
cases.note: Pod names carry hyphens; if `-` were treated as an operator inside a word the predicate would silently invert.

cases.name: quote in a term does not break the literal
cases.note: Injection safety. The assertion is parseability, not a count: `it's` compiles to a phrase search that legitimately matches (2,056 rows measured, since the tokenizer splits on the apostrophe). What must never happen is a syntax error or a broken string literal.

cases.name: literal percent is not a wildcard
cases.note: Verifies the two layers of escaping: LIKE's backslash-percent keeps the percent literal, and the SQL literal doubles the backslash. If Databend does NOT honour backslash escapes inside string literals this case will misbehave — that is exactly what it is here to detect.

cases.name: boolean AND agrees with LIKE
cases.note: Both terms merge into one query() call. Two match() calls would fail [1065] duplicate search function.

cases.name: negation subtracts exactly
cases.note: The name is now the assertion: `peer -status` plus `peer status` must equal `peer` exactly, no rows lost or double-counted. Measured 21,418 + 74,207 = 95,625.

cases.name: fuzzy composes with a structured filter
cases.note: match(...,'fuzziness=1') is the one search function; the column predicate is not one, so they compose.

cases.name: fuzzy composes with LIKE
cases.note: LIKE is not a search function either.
